original_question: Let (X,tau) be a co-sober space and let k:(X,tau)->(X,tau) be continuous such that k:X->X is a kernel operator for the specialization order, meaning k(x) lies in the closure of {x} and k(k(x)) = k(x) for every x. Is the subspace k(X) with the subspace topology again co-sober?

missing_details: To make the problem fully stand-alone, the paper's definition of co-sober should be stated: every k-irreducible compact saturated subset G of X must be of the form ↑x for a unique x ∈ X. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

The T0 assumption is implicit in your draft through the term co-sober; in the paper, co-sobriety is defined only for T0 spaces. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

The notions K(X) and k-irreducible should be unpacked if the question is to stand alone: K(X) denotes the nonempty compact saturated subsets of X, and G is k-irreducible when G = K1 ∪ K2 with K1, K2 ∈ K(X) forces G = K1 or G = K2. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

The specialization order should be made explicit: x ≤X y iff x ∈ cl{y}; then the kernel condition k(x) ∈ cl{x} is equivalently k(x) ≤X x. ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))

For paper-faithful notation, the target should be written as the subspace (k(X), τ|_{k(X)}). ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
refined_question: Let (X, τ) be a T0 space, let ≤X denote its specialization order (x ≤X y iff x ∈ cl{y}), and let K(X) be the set of all nonempty compact saturated subsets of X. Call G ∈ K(X) k-irreducible if G = K1 ∪ K2 with K1, K2 ∈ K(X) implies G = K1 or G = K2. Assume that X is co-sober, meaning that for every k-irreducible G ∈ K(X) there exists a unique x ∈ X such that G = ↑x. If k : (X, τ) → (X, τ) is continuous and satisfies k(x) ∈ cl{x} and k(k(x)) = k(x) for every x ∈ X (equivalently, k : X → X is a kernel operator with respect to the specialization order of X), must the image subspace (k(X), τ|_{k(X)}) be co-sober? ([repository.nie.edu.sg](https://repository.nie.edu.sg/server/api/core/bitstreams/05c40b88-abb7-4333-9d75-1683e771d05e/content))
justification: The draft clearly targets Section 9 rather than the paper's earlier introductory results: the exact official formulation is Question 9.5 on page 16. The immediate nearby context is Definition 9.1, which supplies the needed meaning of co-sober via k-irreducible compact saturated sets, and Theorem 9.2, which gives the closely related closure-operator image result that motivates this kernel-operator follow-up question. So the sharpest paper-faithful rewrite is simply Question 9.5 with those implicit definitions made explicit.
